2607.09053.title: An Emergent Mirage: Is Emergent Misalignment and Realignment Indeed a Robust Phenomenon?
2607.09053.paper_summary: Recent work has reported Emergent Misalignment (EM), where language models fine-tuned on narrow, domain-specific misaligned datasets abruptly acquire broadly misaligned behavior, alongside evidence that this behavior can be reversed through limited realignment. We systematically study repeated alignment and misalignment cycles using controlled fine-tuning loops while tracking behavioral performance, and LoRA representations throughout training. Although we reproduce EM, we find that both misalignment and realignment are highly sensitive to superficial dataset characteristics, with apparent rapid realignment largely disappearing after controlling for response-length differences. We further find that previously reported mechanistic signatures, including representational phase transitions in LoRA space, do not consistently correlate with behavioral misalignment across training. Our results suggest that current evidence for EM is less robust than previously claimed and highlight the need for evaluation protocols that carefully control for these surface level dataset artifacts to identify the robustness of the EM phenomenon.
2607.09053.paper_summary_zh: 最近的研究報告了新興的不一致性（EM），在此情況下，針對狹窄、特定領域的不一致數據集進行微調的語言模型，突然獲得了廣泛的不一致行為，同時有證據表明這種行為可以通過有限的重新調整來逆轉。<lb/>我們系統性地研究了重複的對齊和不對齊循環，使用受控的微調循環，同時跟踪行為表現和訓練過程中的LoRA表示。<lb/>儘管我們重現了EM，但我們發現不一致性和重新調整對表面數據集特徵非常敏感，顯著的快速重新調整在控制響應長度差異後幾乎消失。<lb/>我們進一步發現，先前報告的機械特徵，包括LoRA空間中的表示相變，並未與訓練過程中的行為不一致性穩定相關。<lb/>我們的結果表明，當前對EM的證據不如先前聲稱的那麼穩健，並突顯出需要評估協議，以仔細控制這些表面數據集工件，以識別EM現象的穩健性。
